game_build_compatibility: Measured on the GOG release: exe SHA-256 8F84F4A650BA814CDB6744D2F1CFAE668B887551885176939C71652483A18722 (FileVersion 1.0.2445.0, GOG gameId 1324471032, buildId 55823353107546309). Not the Steam build (1.0.8874.0).
claim: The GOG executable shows none of the Steam build's wrapper indicators: its entry point is in .text and its sections are a conventional MSVC layout, with no .bind section, whereas the Steam build enters in .bind (entropy 7.947, F-ENV-003).
evidence: pe_inventory.py on the GOG exe: entry_point_section .text; sections .text, .interpr, .rdata, .data, .pdata, .gfids, .tls, _RDATA, .SHARED, .rsrc, .reloc; COFF timestamp 2022-08-26; 37 import DLLs including steam_api64.dll. Steam build: entry .bind, 17 sections, COFF timestamp 2018-08-24, 21 import DLLs.
verification_method: Read-only header parsing with the Phase 1 tool tools/environment/pe_inventory.py (the same measurement as F-ENV-003); no code was disassembled, unpacked or executed.
limitations: The absence of the Steam build's wrapper indicators is not a proof that no protection exists. The steam_api64.dll import is expected for a game that uses the Steam API only when present; that it degrades gracefully without Steam is the owner's launch test, not shown here.
next_experiment: The owner's launch without any store client (F-ENV-009); then D-008.
